target_customer: Adult children and family caregivers of older adults
problem: Families struggle to find and vet elder care products and services; ReverCare uses social workers as free guides funded by affiliate fees.
business_model: Affiliate fees from recommended products and services
product_category: Elder care concierge and review site

founders.name: Kiyan Rajabi
education: Technion-Cornell dual master's degrees in Health Tech, 2018

founders.name: Darya Moldavskaya
education: Master of Computer Science, 2018 (Cornell Tech profile)

competitors.name: Lifted
competitors.what: End to end elderly care platform

technical_complexity.rationale: Content, referral and coaching service with little engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Easy to copy; large referral networks already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not copied; ReverCare was acquired by Vibrant Aging in 2022.

market_need_then: Cornell Tech coverage cites the founders' own families struggling with caregiving; Cornell gave it a 2018 startup award.

branding.domain_note: revercare.com; the site is still live.

brand_strength.rationale: Cornell and ILR coverage but no brand level evidence; the name is a blend that some may misspell.

pivots.from: Platform connecting caregivers with expert coaches
pivots.to: Review and affiliate site for elder care products
pivots.why: Site says it began as a coaching platform in 2018 and now reviews products; date not given

outcome_analysis: ReverCare began at Cornell Tech in 2018 as a social worker concierge for family caregivers and raised a small seed round of about 150K dollars through YC and ELabNYC. It became an affiliate review site and was acquired by Vibrant Aging in 2022 with terms undisclosed, a small exit rather than a venture scale outcome. The Inactive label reflects the acquisition, not a failure, and no failure cause is public.
notes: YC status says Inactive while Cornell and PitchBook say acquired by Vibrant Aging in 2022 and the site is live. The 150K seed rests on CB Insights; PitchBook lists 427K total, so a 277K gap remains and Latka reports none. CB Insights names a different founder (Kenneth Wong), a conflict not used. The Lifted source is dated September 2019, about two months after the batch start. Success factor other means a small acquisition, not a venture scale exit.
